title: Throughput & Isolation: Buyer-Focused Elevator Scripts and Negotiation Notes for Dedicated Capacity
body:
Purpose
Provide AEs and solution engineers a compact, buyer-focused set of elevator scripts, objection responses, and negotiation-ready language for selling Redwood Dedicated capacity with predictable throughput, strict tenant isolation, and SLA guarantees. This is intentionally pragmatic: quick soundbites, sample contract language, and a procurement checklist to accelerate deal cycles with infrastructure, platform, and procurement stakeholders.

One-line positioning
Redwood Dedicated gives your ML teams reserved inference capacity with hard throughput guarantees, tenant-level isolation, and predictable unit economics so production apps never hit capacity surprises.

Why this matters to buyers (3 sentence version)
- SREs and platform teams need predictable tail latency and throughput to maintain SLOs for customer-facing features.
- Security and legal teams require provable isolation and auditable behavior for regulated workloads.
- Finance/procurement wants predictable monthly spend and concrete failure modes to price risk. Redwood Dedicated targets all three with contractual SLAs, isolation controls, and a procurement-friendly playbook.

Primary buyer personas and what they care about
- Platform/Infra Lead (CTO/Head of Platform): cares about throughput, SLAs, and integration effort. Signal: asks about sustained QPS and autoscaling behavior.
- SRE/Service Owner: cares about tail latency, failover, and tracing/explainer hooks. Signal: asks about observability, tracing, and incident playbooks.
- Security/Compliance: cares about tenant isolation, network controls, and KMS/HSM integrations. Signal: requests SOC2/ISO artifacts and VPC/private deployment options.
- Procurement/Finance: cares about predictable spend, termination clauses, and penalties for SLA breaches. Signal: asks for sample SOW, pricing bands, and credit calculations.

Three core messaging pillars (short)
1) Predictability: reserved GPU pools + throughput SLAs = no surprise throttling. Callout: guaranteed sustained token throughput per commit tier.
2) Safety & Isolation: strict tenancy separation, private control plane options, and audit logs for compliance teams.
3) Cost Transparency: per-token economics, burst policies, and autoscaling guardrails that limit runaway spend.

Elevator scripts (30s each)
- CTO / Head of Platform: 'If you need production-grade inference that won't degrade during peak traffic, Redwood Dedicated guarantees throughput and isolation so your engineers can ship features without adding complex infra. We surface token-level cost and latency so you can optimize economics continuously.'
- SRE / Reliability Lead: 'We commit to sustained throughput and an incident playbook with canary rollbacks and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. You get per-route latency dashboards, tracing hooks, and a defined SLA credit calculation for outages.'
- Security / Compliance Lead: 'We offer private control plane options, VPC peering, and KMS/HSM integrations along with audit logs for every inference call. For air-gapped requirements, we have an on-prem packaging option and a signed attestation process.'
- Procurement / Finance: 'We provide reserved capacity contracts with fixed monthly commitments, clear burst policies, and a simple formula for SLA credits. We can provide a sample SOW and a procurement-ready pricing appendix within 48 hours.'

Common objections and suggested responses
- Objection: 'We can just use cloud instances or another vendor.'
  Response: 'Cloud instances shift operational risk to your team; Redwood combines a tuned runtime, workload-aware batching, and an orchestration layer that reduces unit cost while giving SLA-backed throughput and isolation out of the box.'
- Objection: 'How do you guarantee isolation if we're sharing hardware?'
  Response: 'Isolation is enforced at the runtime layer and via reserved pools for Dedicated customers. For regulated workloads we offer physical pool assignment and private control plane options that meet common audit requirements.'
- Objection: 'We need predictable spend, not usage spikes.'
  Response: 'Reserved commitments set a baseline; we define burst windows and soft quota alerts. The contract includes clear overage rules and an option for burst credits to avoid surprise bills.'

Sample SLA language snippets (procurement-ready)
- Throughput commitment: 'Redwood will provide a minimum sustained throughput of X tokens/sec (p50/p95 thresholds) for the agreed reserved capacity tier during the Term. Measured throughput will be per-customer aggregate across allocated GPU pool(s).'
- Latency SLO and remediation: 'Redwood commits to 95th percentile request latency under Y ms for prompt lengths up to Z tokens. Failure to meet the p95 latency target for two consecutive billing periods entitles Customer to a service credit calculated as 5% of monthly fees per missed period, up to a total of 50%.'
- Isolation warranty: 'Redwood warrants that Dedicated capacity will maintain tenant isolation such that Customer compute and state are prevented from co-mingling with other customers. For customers electing physical isolation, Redwood will provision separate physical GPU pools for the duration of the Term.'
- Outage definition and credits: 'Outage is defined as a period when Customer requests receive HTTP 5xx responses at a rate exceeding 10% of total requests for more than 5 consecutive minutes. Credit calculation: (Downtime minutes / Total minutes in billing period) * Monthly fee * 0.75.'

Procurement redlines to anticipate (fast checklist)
- Ask for concrete measurement windows and observability endpoints (how will throughput be measured)
- Push back on open-ended termination for convenience; replace with phased exit plan and data handoff timeline
- Validate isolation wording: physical pool vs logical enforcement, and what audit artifacts are delivered
- Confirm escalation and incident response SLAs (pager contacts, escalation matrix)
- Overage and burst pricing: require specific caps or pre-purchased burst credit packs

Competitive differentiation (short analysis)
- General cloud GPU endpoints: cheaper raw infrastructure but require significant engineering to tune runtime and manage KV cache, batching, and model fallbacks. Redwood packages that expertise with operational guarantees.
- LLM API providers: strong on model quality and simplicity but weaker on isolation and committed throughput at enterprise scale. Redwood focuses on serving economics and predictable capacity.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes: maximum control but high ops cost and longer time-to-market. Redwood Dedicated aims for a middle path: ops-lite with contractual guarantees.

Negotiation playbook for AEs (tactical steps)
1) Discovery: confirm peak QPS, tail latency tolerance, and compliance requirements. Capture requested measurement metrics verbatim.
2) Offer: propose a tier with reserved capacity matching 80-120% of observed peak sustained throughput plus a defined small burst window.
3) Optional add-ons: private control plane, physical pool isolation, extended SLA credits (for extra fee).
4) Contracting: provide standard SOW + pricing appendix; highlight sample SLA snippets and a 60-day tech integration milestone.
5) Close: include 30-day performance review with option to resize pool without penalty at renewal.

Pricing worked example (illustrative)
- Customer baseline: sustained need 10k tokens/sec during peak, p95 latency target 300ms.
- Redwood recommended commit: Dedicated Tier C (12k sustained), monthly fee $120k. Burst policy: additional 50% burst capacity for up to 10 hours/month at blended overage rate.
- SLA: p95 latency < 300ms; remediation credit equals 5% monthly fee per missed billing period.

Technical appendix to reference in RFP responses
- Measurement methodology: throughput measured at the API ingress after queuing, averaged over 1-minute windows, with aggregation across allocated workers.
- Observability deliverables: per-route latency histograms, token counts, error rates, and KV cache hit rates; CSV export for billing reconciliation.
- Isolation artifacts: tenant assignment manifests, audit logs for inference requests, and optional physical pool assignment certificates.

AE play checklist before handing to legal/procurement
- Confirm the exact throughput measurement window the customer will use for acceptance tests
- Lock in isolation requirement (logical vs physical) and map to pricing impact
- Prepare a sample SOW that includes integration milestones and rollback triggers
- Create a joint runbook draft with customer SREs to cover failover and canary policies

Next steps / quick tasks
- Create two slide variants: 1) executive summary for procurement, 2) technical appendix for SRE/security (owner: Evan, due 2025-12-05)
- Draft a short redline-friendly SOW template with the SLA snippets above (owner: Mariana, due 2025-12-03)
- Record two 5-minute roleplay videos for AE enablement using the elevator scripts (owner: Samir, due 2025-12-08)

Notes and open questions
- Decide whether to include a formal performance warranty for offline model regressions (tradeoff legal exposure vs commercial confidence).
- Need legal to sign off on the credit caps in the outage calculation and the definition of outage (owner: legal).

Attachments to prepare

- Short integration checklist for platform teams
